tools.name: get_next_earnings
tools.description: Next earnings report date for one US ticker: report_date, BMO/AMC timing, status, confidence, source_url. Always state the status: 'confirmed' is company-announced (cite source_url); 'estimated' is a projection, never present it as confirmed. Paid plans add `behaviour`: this company's past announcem

tools.name: list_earnings
tools.description: Earnings events in a date window (max 120 days), filtered by status, cap_bucket (small, mid, large, mega), timing (BMO, AMC) or one of the caller's watchlists (name or id; see list_watchlists). Relay each event's status, cite source_url for confirmed dates, and label estimated dates as projections.

tools.name: get_date_changes
tools.description: Earnings dates that moved, were confirmed, went into conflict or were reported since an ISO timestamp, with old and new date and status and the source_url behind each; cite it. Filters: ticker, cap_bucket, watchlist. Oldest first; when has_more is true, call again with since = next_since.

tools.name: get_earnings_history
tools.description: Past earnings release dates for one ticker: weekday, BMO/AMC timing, days after quarter end, and the EDGAR filing behind each (source_url). Use it to judge how regular the company's cadence is.

tools.name: get_data_coverage
tools.description: How far back data goes for one ticker: release count, first and last release, a count per year, whether releases rest on 8-K Item 2.02 or 10-Q/10-K filings, and when tracking began. Use it before asking for long histories.

tools.name: get_earnings_results
tools.description: Earnings releases for one ticker: revenue and EPS (GAAP and non-GAAP) read by software from the press release, each with its sentence; guidance sentences; call time; exhibit URL. Figures can be wrong: quote the sentence, cite source_url, relay disagrees_with_xbrl and the accuracy block. A null carri

tools.name: get_guidance
tools.description: Guidance statements for one ticker by release, newest first (beta): the verbatim sentence and the exhibit URL. metric, low, high and period_guided are filled only when the sentence states metric, scale and period, otherwise null with a reason. Quote the sentence, cite the exhibit, verify any number

tools.name: get_fundamentals
tools.description: Financial statements for one ticker from its XBRL filings, per quarter or year: revenue, gross profit, operating and net income, diluted EPS and shares, cash flow, capex, free cash flow, cash, debt, assets, liabilities, equity. Each number names its us-gaap tag and accession; cite them. Nulls say wh

tools.name: get_fact
tools.description: Raw time series of one us-gaap concept for a ticker (e.g. Revenues, NetIncomeLoss, EarningsPerShareDiluted, Assets), each value with period, form, filing date and accession. Use for exact filed figures; cite the accession. Unknown concepts return the list of stored ones.

tools.name: get_insider_trades
tools.description: Insider transactions for one ticker from Form 4 filings: owner, role, transaction code, shares, price, holdings after, footnotes, filing URL. Optional since date. around_earnings=true: trades within window_days (default 30) of each past report date. One row per reporting owner; group by accession an

tools.name: get_filings
tools.description: Filing index for one ticker from EDGAR: accession, form, filing and period dates, 8-K items, document URL. Filter by form (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 4, ...) and a since date. Use it to find the exact filing to cite.

tools.name: list_watchlists
tools.description: The caller's watchlists with their tickers. Watchlists belong to the account behind the API key; pass a list's name (or id) as the `watchlist` argument of list_earnings or get_date_changes to answer questions like 'what on my list reports this week'.

tools.name: set_watchlist
tools.description: Create the named watchlist, or replace its tickers if it exists. Tickers outside the covered universe are kept and reported in `unknown`. Free accounts: 1 list of 25 tickers; paid plans: 5 lists of 500.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_next_earnings" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
